skill.displayName: 标讯 · 广东招标中标与招投标数据查询

version.changelog: 首发：垂直版，预置本方向检索配方与关键词命中量对照

llm.summary: The skill mostly supports tender-data searches, but it also handles account creation, device fingerprinting, saved API keys, login links, and promotional/server-supplied messages in ways users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads ZLBX_API_KEY, reads ~/.zlbx/config.json, and if no key is present asks consent to collect platform, CPU architecture, and a stable MAC-address hash for external transmission. That is disclosed, but it is broader than the minimum needed for tender-data queries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package appears to be Markdown documentation only, with no executable installer or bundled scripts. Runtime behavior still directs the agent to make REST calls, read environment/config credentials, and create a local config file during onboarding.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include real scope ambiguity: the manifest says Guangdong is the default region, while the query rules say the default region is national. The skill also instructs verbatim forwarding of server-provided update notices and appending affiliated service referrals for broad routine use cases.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists returned API keys in plaintext at ~/.zlbx/config.json without specifying restrictive file permissions or symlink protections, and it can print an auto-login SID bearer link into chat for quota recharge. No system service, scheduled task, backdoor, or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Tender search, company analysis, market analysis, account balance checks, and paid API access are coherent with the stated purpose, but the automatic registration, recharge login, MAC-derived device fingerprinting, and affiliated-product referral behavior materially expand the skill beyond data lookup.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this vendor receiving a hashed device identifier during automatic registration, storing an API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json, and showing recharge login links in chat. The safer path is to create/configure the API key manually, keep the config file owner-only, avoid bulk contact collection, and treat any server-provided update notice or promotional referral as untrusted information.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The auto-registration and recharge workflow is disclosed and partially consent-gated, but it adds account provisioning, credential issuance, local secret storage, and recovery/recharge handling beyond the core tender-search function.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The Guangdong default conflict is supported by the artifact: the manifest says Guangdong default, while SKILL.md line 267 says national default. This is a material scope ambiguity rather than malicious behavior.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The error table directs auto-registration for invalid, expired, or disabled keys, which weakens the earlier no-key-only gate and could create unintended new accounts instead of stopping for explicit reauthorization.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The MAC-address hash collection and external transmission are real and disclosed, with consent required before initial collection, but the unsalted stable hardware-derived identifier is not necessary for the tender-analysis task itself.
[E1] unexpected: The external POST examples are part of the documented registration flow, not hidden exfiltration code, but they operationalize transmission of host-derived onboarding metadata to the vendor.
[RA2] expected: Local reuse of an API key is purpose-aligned for an API-backed skill, but the documented plaintext ~/.zlbx/config.json persistence lacks permission and secret-store controls.
[SQP-2] expected: Company contact lookup is aligned with procurement and sales intelligence use cases, and the artifact includes masking, no WebSearch completion, and no bulk-export limits; users still need privacy and acceptable-use care.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language documentation matches a China/Guangdong tender-data skill and does not show security-relevant deception; this finding was downgraded to a locale/documentation note.
[T01] unexpected: The static finding about affiliated-product promotion is supported: the skill requires a once-per-session referral for broad ordinary analysis intents, though it is bounded and suppressible when the user asks for only data.
[T01] unexpected: The static finding about skill_update_notice is supported: the skill tells the agent to relay arbitrary server-provided text verbatim once, without validation or length/domain constraints.
[other] unexpected: The MAC-derived device fingerprint transmission is supported by the artifact and is consent-gated, but remains a privacy-sensitive onboarding mechanism.
[T09] unexpected: Plaintext API-key persistence and chat-visible auto-login SID URLs are supported by the artifact and are credential-handling weaknesses rather than evidence of malware.
